findings: Supervisor registration (application.ex:52) is idiomatic and matches this repo's established one-supervisor-per-subsystem convention: `{Task.Supervisor, name: Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor}` is registered the same way as SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor (line 43) and PluginTaskSupervisor (line 45) -- plain child spec, no custom start_link wrapper, comment above it states the rationale for not reusing PluginTaskSupervisor instead of adding it silently. No start-order dependency exists (unlike SandboxPool's documented ordering requirement), and none was needed here, so its placement after PluginRegistry is fine.

Control-flow duplication vs plugin_interface.ex (async_nolink + yield + shutdown + handle_yield_result) is real but justified, not a crutch: REQ-155's own requirement text explicitly told ELIXIR-DEV to 'reuse that shape rather than inventing a second one,' and the design (approved by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR) chose a separate supervisor with a stated reason -- distinct crash/telemetry namespace for a hot-path subsystem executing tenant Lua source directly vs. in-process plugin dispatch. handle_yield_result/3 is intentionally not extracted into a shared helper because its match arms are typed against Executor's five-arm return union, not PluginInterface's two-arm outcome() -- a shared extraction would need a common contract neither module has, which would be premature abstraction for two current call sites. Reasonable as-is; if a third subsystem needs this shape, that would be the trigger to extract a shared Task.Supervisor+yield+shutdown helper, not now.

No scope creep found: diff touches only executor.ex, application.ex, config/config.exs, config/test.exs, and executor_test.exs -- exactly REQ-155's owned_modules. capabilities.ex/platform.ex untouched as instructed. No memory-limiting (REQ-156) code present. No premature abstraction (behaviours/macros) introduced beyond what LUA-10 layer 2 needs.

Decision-record consistency confirmed: decision 0014 (lines 208-209, 411-417) states the LUA-08/LUA-10 pairing requires both an in-band :max_instructions limit and an out-of-band supervising-process kill, and requires a test proving a script that traps its own budget error and continues is still killed by the host layer -- exactly what T2 implements. REQ-154's settled config/API shape (execute_with_manifest/2,3, :max_instructions option) is extended, not re-decided: /3 now additionally requires :timeout_ms with no default, /2's public signature is unchanged, and all real call sites (lua_script_audit.ex) use only the unchanged /2 arity.

Goto-loop test substitution (T2, executor_test.exs:296-332) is well-documented: a 21-line comment block explains why the design's literal pcall-then-loop-again script would not have distinguished layer-2-present from layer-2-removed against this runtime (the :max_instructions counter stays permanently exhausted after tripping), and why the goto construct is the genuine escape hatch layer 1 cannot see. This is exactly the kind of deviation record a future maintainer needs and SECURITY-REVIEWER already independently verified the mechanical claim against the vendored runtime source. It belongs here (not deferred to TEST-DESIGNER) because it is the acceptance-proving test ELIXIR-DEV was required to deliver per REQ-155's own AC list, not exploratory coverage -- TEST-DESIGNER's later pass may still add supplementary coverage on top.

General test quality in executor_test.exs is good: `async: true` is safe (no shared state, no DB), each test is self-contained with inline setup, names map directly to AC numbers (AC-1..AC-7 plus a regression guard), timing-based tests (AC-1, T3, T6) use generous margins and explicit rationale against CI jitter, and T3/T6 assert real process/child-set state rather than trusting the caller's return value alone. No flakiness signals (ELIXIR-DEV's handoff reports a 3x reseed re-run, 24/24 each time).
result.verdict: PASS. No blockers. No rework required.
